question: The header's Sources field names hsdd/context/prd-simple-login.md (US-1, US-2, Demo accounts, Scope) and hsdd/context/update-1-add-phone.md (Change: AC-2.1 amended, AC-2.4; Demo accounts; Scope), both superseded by PRD v2 (Q-032, Q-048). How does the citation touch move them, and does the moved entry also gain the PRD v2 sections the node's own text now cites?

options.label: one PRD v2 entry, each section to its counterpart
options.consequence: The header reads byte for byte as the root's embedded copy S12 wrote (DEC-107), so nothing differs before H15's version ripple. The field still lacks sections the Overview and Isolation strategy cite (Constraints, Team and delivery, Rooms, US-4 to US-6) until H14 adds them.

options.label: one PRD v2 entry, plus the newly cited sections
options.consequence: The field is complete now, but the touch adds citations rather than moving them, and the header then differs from the embedded copy, which this step cannot write, until H15.

chosen: one PRD v2 entry, each section to its counterpart
why: hsdd-spec's citation touch moves a node's Sources entry for a source document to the current version and changes only citations. PRD v2's header supersedes prd-simple-login.md together with update-1-add-phone.md, so one entry replaces both. PRD 1's US-1, US-2, Demo accounts and Scope have PRD v2 sections of the same names; Update 1's Change (AC-2.1 amended, AC-2.4) sits inside PRD v2 US-2 (AC-2.1 and AC-2.4 read as Update 1 left them, AC-2.1 now with time zone), its Demo accounts and Scope are PRD v2's. The union is (US-1, US-2, Demo accounts, Scope), the mapping S12 used for the embedded copy. The intake record's Sources and Scope paragraph gives the newly governing sections to each phase-plan-append, so they are routed to H14 as a consider. Had the intake record left the additions to the citation touch, the second option would have led.

question: The file cites profile-api@v1 seven times: the header's Produces line, the Overview ('Everything it promises the web app is in auth-api@v1 and profile-api@v1, which simple-login.backend.3 replaces with profile-api@v2, and in booking-api@v1'), simple-login.backend.2's Produces, simple-login.backend.3's Scope twice and Verification once, and the phase graph's B2 to integration.1 edge. profile-api@v1 is stable, not deprecated, coexisting with v2. What does the touch do with them, and where does the one consider item go, given that Q-047 already carries the root's ten such citations to this node?

options.label: leave all seven; one consider to simple-login.backend, folding Q-047
options.consequence: The planner of this node's next phases (H14) and its reconcile (H15) see one item that covers the root's and this file's v1 citations and names profile-api@v2; Q-047 closes as explained, its text kept in the new item.

options.label: leave all seven; a separate consider, Q-047 left open
options.consequence: Two items on the same subject reach H14; Q-047 stays open although it was routed to this step, which the dispatch's closes rule does not allow.

options.label: restate the Overview sentence to name profile-api@v2 only
options.consequence: Moves a citation of a live earlier version, which the citation-touch rule forbids, and drops the true statement that v1 is what simple-login.backend.2 shipped.

chosen: leave all seven; one consider to simple-login.backend, folding Q-047
why: hsdd-spec's citation touch: an earlier version that is neither deprecated nor retired stays live beside the new one, so every citation of it is left and one consider item naming the new version goes to the node whose plan would move to it. The Produces line is never moved in any case (hsdd-reconcile's version ripple writes it), and four of the seven sit in shipped phases (verification docs for simple-login.backend.2 and simple-login.backend.3 on main), which are history in full. The Overview sentence stays true against current text: profile-api@v2 Versioning says GET /api/me carries one shape and serves v2 only from the v2 phase on, which is 'replaces'. The producer is this node, so the item targets simple-login.backend; Q-047 says the same of the root's copies, and one item keeps H14's input single. A consumer still planning a phase on v1 would have made that consumer the target.

question: Q-027 to Q-031 target H14, simple-login.backend's phase-plan-append, and reached this citation touch only because H14's target is the same node; the step must close every routed item, and a closed item no longer reaches H14. How are they closed?

options.label: close each as explained and carry its text to H14
options.consequence: H14 receives every item whole with the same kind (Q-028 stays must-address); the queue gains five new ids, the churn DEC-087 already logged as an hsdd-auto defect.

options.label: close each as addressed
options.consequence: Claims work this step did not do: a citation touch changes only citations, and every item is Phase Plan content; H14 would never see them.

chosen: close each as explained and carry its text to H14
why: hsdd-spec's citation touch changes only citations and the sentences they sit in, so none of these plan items (the time model in PostgreSQL, the replay rig's clock and given, booking-api@v1's guarantees for the plan, the timeZone tests, the test database) can be addressed here, and the dispatch requires every routed item closed. S09, S10 and S11 met the same mechanics and the orchestrator kept the carry (DEC-085, DEC-087, DEC-095, DEC-103). Each carried text keeps the item's original text verbatim, so its trail back to S04, S05, S07 and S09 survives. A way for an item on H14 to wait for H14 would have changed this.

question: How does this citation touch classify against the touched artifact's own versioning rules?

options.label: compatible wording change, nothing versioned moves
options.consequence: The node keeps its id, Kind, Consumes, Produces, Governed by, phases and Phase Plan; no contract or ADR file changes, so neither INDEX is regenerated.

options.label: a change for hsdd-reconcile to drain
options.consequence: Would add a Governance updates entry for a Sources move that no contract or consumer can observe.

chosen: compatible wording change, nothing versioned moves
why: hsdd-spec asks for the classification as one decision. Only the header's Sources line changed (DEC-117): two baseline entries became one PRD v2 entry with the same sections' counterparts. Kind, Purpose, Owns, Does not own, Consumes, Produces, Governed by, Decomposes into, Isolation strategy, Overview and the whole Phase Plan are byte for byte as before; no sentence was restated. A node spec has no version of its own, and a Sources entry is context for the next skill, not something a consumer reads. Had a Produces or Consumes line needed to change, it would have gone to hsdd-reconcile instead.

question: S13 moved the backend's Sources line, kept twelve citations as history or live, and carried five items to H14 (B-10). Keep the output or rework?

options.label: Keep the output
options.consequence: The backend's header matches its root copy; the carried items reach H14 with their text and kind.

options.label: Rework
options.consequence: No different result is available; the carrying follows from B-10 (DEC-087).

why: The diff is one Sources line, matching the root's copy exactly; every kept citation is in a shipped phase, a dated append paragraph or a live earlier version. The reads outside are inside the repository; none is out of bounds. A moved citation inside a shipped phase would have changed this.
